subject: Business
title: Hyperbolic Discounting: Now vs. Later
description: A short lesson to help you apply Hyperbolic Discounting: Now vs. Later.

hook.text: Would you rather have $100 today or $110 tomorrow? Most take the $100. But $100 in 30 days or $110 in 31? They wait.

buildup.text: Hyperbolic discounting means we massively overvalue immediate rewards compared to future ones.

discovery.text: This is why people skip retirement saving. The pleasure of spending now dwarfs the abstract future gain.

twist.text: The bias disappears with distance. We plan to start dieting on Monday but never on today.

climax.text: Commitment devices work: auto-transfer to savings, gym contracts, public pledges.

punchline.text: We're patient about the future. Just not about right now.

quiz.question: What is hyperbolic discounting?
options: Overvaluing immediate rewards relative to future ones
Discounting products based on demand curves
A pricing strategy for digital goods

details.summary: Hyperbolic discounting describes the human preference for smaller immediate rewards over larger future ones, even when waiting is objectively better. People choose one hundred dollars today over one hundred twenty in a month but are indifferent between them a year from now.
details.whyItMatters: This bias explains why people undersave for retirement, procrastinate on important projects, and choose instant gratification over long-term goals. Businesses exploit it through buy-now-pay-later schemes and immediate reward programs.
takeaways: People disproportionately prefer immediate rewards over larger future ones
The discount rate is steepest for near-term delays, flattening over time
Commitment devices help overcome hyperbolic discounting for better outcomes

faq.question: How does hyperbolic discounting affect retirement saving?
faq.answer: People value spending today far more than saving for a distant retirement. Each pay period, the immediate pleasure of spending outweighs the abstract future benefit. Automatic enrollment defaults and escalation programs overcome this by making saving the path of least resistance.

faq.question: What is a commitment device and how does it help?
faq.answer: A commitment device is a voluntary constraint that limits future choices to overcome present bias. Examples include automatic savings transfers, public goal announcements, and apps that donate to charity if you miss targets. They bind your future self to your current intentions.
